about: A proposed mapping of products on CISA's known-exploited list to classes of use, as the first step towards totals by sector. A proposal, not sector exposure: it says what kind of product an entry concerns, not who uses it, and nothing about Portugal's infrastructure.
notice: Proposal, not sector exposure. Weak signals, not an audit. Counts are CVEs on CISA KEV per class of product; a general-IT CVE concerns every sector at once, so the classes are never summed into sectors.
from: Dinis Cruz's answer on 18 November 2026, about 23:41 UTC, when asked about publishing a mapping of products to sectors: "I think that sounds quite good". He has not approved this mapping.

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.note: This mapping is ours; the vendor and product names are CISA KEV's, as served.

precedence: A rule for a vendor and product beats a rule for the whole vendor; anything no rule matches is not classed yet.

classes.name: Industrial and building control
classes.reason: Controllers, operator panels and their engineering software are used to run plants, networks and buildings, not offices.

classes.name: General IT
classes.reason: General-purpose software and devices (operating systems, browsers, office and collaboration software, network and security appliances, enterprise and developer software) that organisations of every kind run; nothing in these entries ties them to one sector.

rules.evidence: NVD CPEs: siemens simatic_cp_1543-1_firmware, siplus_net_cp_1543-1_firmware
rules.reason: A communication processor (CP 1543-1) for SIMATIC industrial controllers, as the NVD product names say.

rules.evidence: NVD CPEs: rockwellautomation rslogix_5000, studio_5000_logix_designer, factorytalk_services_platform
rules.reason: The entry concerns Rockwell Automation's Logix controller software and FactoryTalk; only this entry is classed, not every Rockwell product.

rules.evidence: NVD CPEs: unitronics vision and samba PLC/HMI firmware, visilogic
rules.reason: Programmable logic controllers with operator panels; only this entry is classed.

rules.evidence: NVD CPE: deltaww dopsoft
rules.reason: Design software for Delta's industrial operator panels (HMI).

rules.evidence: NVD CPE: schneider-electric u.motion_builder
rules.reason: Configuration software for U.motion building automation, as the product name says: building control, not office IT.

rules.evidence: computed: the distinct products of this vendor on CISA KEV now (shown beside the rule)
rules.reason: A vendor of general-purpose IT: its products on the list are used across every sector.
